'''Solange Magalhães''' is a painter.<ref>{{cite news|title=Um aceno ao ônibus da esquina  |url=http://www2.uol.com.br/JC/_2001/1609/ale1609.htm|accessdate=8 December 2010|newspaper=[[:pt:JC online|JC Online]]|date=16 September 2001|language=Portuguese|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20030418043125/http://www2.uol.com.br/JC/_2001/1609/ale1609.htm|archive-date=18 April 2003}}</ref>

She was born in [[France]] in 1939. Her family moved to [[Rio de Janeiro]], [[Brazil]] when she was 13 years old. In 1963, after three years of studying theoretical physics, she chose to be a painter.

She has experimented with various painting techniques – oil, acrylic, watercolor, India ink – on different materials such as canvas, paper and [[masonite]].

Her first solo exhibition took place in 1968 at the [[Galeria Goeldi]] in Rio, invited by the art-critic [[Clarival do Prado Valladares]] and introduced by writer [[Clarice Lispector]].{{Citation needed|date=July 2011}} Since that time her work has been shown in numerous solo and group shows in the major Brazilian cities of Rio de Janeiro, [[Recife]] and [[São Paulo]], as well as in [[Germany]] and [[France]].{{Citation needed|date=July 2011}}

Of particular note was the 1980 exhibition at the [[Studien Galerie]] at [[Stuttgart University]] in Germany, invited by its director, professor [[Max Bense]], and two exhibitions in Rio: ''Solange Magalhães, 30 Years of Painting, a Circular Vision of the World'' at the [[Museu Nacional de Belas Artes|Fine Arts Museum]] in Rio de Janeiro (1995); and ''From Chaos to Cosmos'' at the [[Espaço Cultural Correios]] (2007).{{Citation needed|date=July 2011}}
